item.title: Digital Decision Accelerators for Defence (DDAD), UK6 Contract Award Notification (CAN)
item.description:
The Ministry of Defence (MOD) has concluded its procurement process for a new Defence and Security Open Framework, specifically created to foster a deep eco-system for advanced digital decision-supporting capabilities. An Open Framework is a scheme of successive framework iterations that are periodically re-opened (competed) under substantially unchanged terms.

For the avoidance of doubt within this published CAN, as an Open Framework the listed Suppliers are subject to change following a framework reopening. When this occurs, the Authority will communicate this update with industry via updating this notice or issuing a new one with an updated Framework Member list. 

This Open Framework will serve as the primary delivery route for ASGARD; the British Army's flagship Transformative Capability Initiative (TCI). ASGARD forms a central componennt of the Chief of the General Staff's Growth Through Transformation (GTT) Strategy. The DDAD Framework may be used as agreed to procure other, non-ASGARD, goods and services.

The Framework will operate for an initial four (4) core year period, with optional extensions detailed elsewhere. 

The maximum throughput of the framework during the 'Core' period is £180,000,000 (Ex. VAT). This figure represents a ceiling ("Headroom") of spend rather than any spending commitment. 

The MOD has carefully considered its approach to 'lots', and detailed of SME considerations were issued in previous publications. The Structure and process was designed to be accessible, and this has been successful in that 50% of suppliers (14 out of 26) are UK- based SMEs.

In total, twenty-six (26) suppliers were successful. Six (6) of these Suppliers secured placed on two (2) lots - the maximum allowed.

item.title: Research and Evaluation Framework
item.description:
This is a Contract Award Notice.

The Care Quality Commission (CQC) is conducting this procurement to set up a new multi supplier research framework using the Open Procedure in accordance with requirements of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 for the purpose of procuring health and social care research and evaluation services. CQC are seeking tenders from relevant providers to deliver the services which are divided into Lots identified within the procurement documents.

Framework Part A - Call Off Partnerships
Lot 1: Research partner.
Lot 2: Academic partner.
Lot 3: Consultation partner.

Framework Part B - Thematic Lots
Lot 4: Safety and improvement in health and social care.
Lot 5: Reducing inequalities in health and social care.
Lot 6: Local health and social care systems, integration and joined-up care.
Lot 7: Involving people in health and social care and understanding people's experiences of care.
Lot 8: Organisational improvement and culture.
Lot 9: Effective social care.

Framework Part C - Methodological Lots
Lot 10: Polling and surveys.
Lot 11: Artificial Intelligence.

The Framework will be for an initial period of 24 months with an option to extend for up to 24 months.

For Lots 1 to 3, only one single supplier will be appointed for each Lot. There will be a different awarded supplier for each Lot. A supplier cannot be awarded more than one Lot in Lots 1 to 3.

For Lots 4 to 10, the Authority seeks to award up to a maximum of fifteen Suppliers per Lot. A supplier may be awarded to one or multiple Lots.

For Lot 11 the Authority seeks to award up to a maximum of five Suppliers.

Contract Reference: CQC EP&S 052

item.title: Advanced Analytics (Taskforce 2019)
item.description:
The supplier will conduct analyses and develop decision support tools for policymakers regarding the likely impact of the Covid-19 outbreak on business and industry. These tools will be used to inform policy decisions and prioritise funding to vulnerable businesses, sectors or geographies, and monitor business closures and impacts in near real-time.
Successful delivery of this research and tooling will require the following analytical capabilities:

1.	Application of machine learning across alternative data sources to forecast and monitor the impact of Covid-19 across business and industry by sector and geography
2.	Simulation to estimate likely future impact of Covid-19 across business and industry
3.	Development of interactive applications/dashboards which summarise the above monitoring and forecasting activities into an easily consumable interface to inform policy-makers

At present a cross-functional team from within BEIS is being assembled from experts in the Economics and Data Science practices. Faculty is proposing to support the BEIS internal team with a high-performing group of data scientists, engineers and UI/UX designers to work directly alongside BEIS to deliver these capabilities.
The intention is for this to work as a single team, working in a highly agile and iterative way; potentially shifting towards clearer work streams or deliverables as the user requirements sharpen in focus. The team will work under direction of BEIS on a time-and-materials basis, with an estimated project duration of between 3 and 6 months

item.title: National Biosurveillance Network Discovery (Ref C113285)
item.description:
The NBN is a government initiative, supported by Cabinet Office, brought about by the re-evaluation of the biosecurity risk landscape, which considers the evolving priorities since COVID-19 and the rapid advances in science and technology.

Whilst investment in biosecurity, science and technology remains high across government departments this challenge is in building a connected network around these programmes that enables the fast detection of threats in our environment as and when they occur.

UKHSA want to understand the picture across Government, where the gaps are, how we fill them and create a coherent network to deliver functional biosurveillance. Achieving this understanding through NBN discovery will allow for business case creation (for alpha, beta and final phases that will span this FY and the next two), explaining how we get from where we are now, to where we need to be.

item.title: NPCC ANPR Analytics Tool
item.description:
The AAT identifies vehicles of interest (VOIs) by using the National ANPR System (NAS). The AAT allows users to upload NAS exported .CSVs and, once processed, it provides analysis on the data by identifying VOIs and unusual patterns. Analysts can then create intelligence packs to inform local police on potential County lines related stop and search opportunities. 

The tool was trialled by the North West (NW) ROCU in 2022 and then, due to significant increases in the success rate of CL-related stop and searches, the trial was expanded in 2024 under Operation Ignition to an additional 2 ROCUs - Yorkshire & Humber (YH) and South East (SE) ROCUs. During that second trial, areas of tool development were identified, alongside the need for further ML in order that the tool could be made more widely available across all ROCUs and other crime types in the future. 

This Machine Learning (ML) phase will ensure that the AAT can deliver region specific insights into County lines and provide the evidence required to inform future national adoption.

item.title: AISI Safeguard Surveys Partner
item.description:
As part of its mission to measure and improve the security of frontier AI systems, AISI is developing risk assessments that identify how the defences of frontier AI system might be subverted by attackers. These threat models summarize the risk from abuse violations in LLM-based models, where model capabilities are used to aid in criminal or otherwise undesirable behaviour.  

To support AISI in creating these threat models, AISI seeks a partner to map the attack surfaces, attack vectors, and system safeguards of selected closed-source advanced AI systems. The chosen partner will be a significant strategic collaborator of AISI's Safeguards team, directly contributing key information to AISI's models of system security.

item.title: Procurement for the Provision of an Urgent and Emergency Care Live Dashboard and CTCC Strategic Partner to BNSSG ICB
item.description:
NHS Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) CCG has been reviewing its capability for online tools supporting our daily Urgent and Emergency Care system management and escalation, or our OPEL framework. We are assessing the market for a provider who can take and display relevant live or near real time data feeds from our UEC partners (including and not limited to acute, community, ambulance, 111, AWP, social care, voluntary).
Historically in BNSSG, we have used third party providers to data warehouse and manage daily un-validated provider performance and activity information. This information has supported us with our daily system management and escalation actions. However, as a health and social care system we have digitally matured over the past few years  having developed our own PowerBI reporting functionality, and therefore no longer require support with warehousing and reporting this information (including but not limited to: ECDS, National A&E Sitreps, Ambulance Daily and Weekly, NHS 111, Long Stays, COVID-19 SITREPs).

In addition, BNSSG are seeking to work in strategic partnership with a supplier to deliver a platform that provides real-time visualisations of activity, patient flow, harm and the impact of initiatives within BNSSG to facilitate evidence- based decision making. This will optimise resource, remove barriers and improve patient outcomes for our population. 

BNSSG have completed a proof of concept and a prototype data visualisation which can be viewed as part of the tender documentation.

We are in process of developing the Beta and anticipate rollout of the live basic product in Q4 22/23, with continued development in the 23/24.

The contract will be for 2 years with the option to extend for up to two further years. The financial envelope is:

•	Year 1: £241,600 +VAT  
•	Year 2: £141,600 +VAT 

Optional extensions:

•	Year 3: £141,600 +VAT 
•	Year 4: £141,600 +VAT

Bidders should be prepared to outline how this would be split between delivery of the core product and ongoing development of the Care Traffic Coordination Centre Tool.  

The procurement will follow a two stage, restricted process and interested providers can register and download the pre-qualification documents from our e-procurement system, Atamis at https://health-family.force.com/s/Welcome. The closing deadline for responses is 12 noon on the 31st October 2022.

item.title: Medical IT
item.description:
NHS Supply Chain seeks to establish a non-exclusive framework agreement for supply to the NHS Supply Chain customer base via the Direct Route. NHS Supply Chain intends to launch a national framework agreement for the provision of medical IT software solutions for example departmental IT solutions such as radiology, pathology, cardiology, endoscopy, mammography, electronic patient records and sharing solutions, within an NHS hospital, NHS community and/or social care environment. Also included is the provision of medical IT hardware. This includes but is not limited to servers, monitors and workstations. More details can be found within Appendix 3 framework agreement specification.

It is anticipated that in the first 24 months of the framework agreement the value of purchases will be circa GBP 282 717 625.93 however this is approximate only. The figures for the total estimated value are based on that initial expenditure and include a forecast for growth.

item.title: Technical analysis and comparison of approaches to bias identification and mitigation in decision making algorithms
item.description: With particular reference to approaches within financial services and recruitment, The Centre for Data Ethics and Innovation (CDEI) is commissioning a piece of research analysing, assessing and comparing the various approaches to bias mitigation as well as providing detailed technical standards which could be used to identify bias and means for mitigating bias. We will use the outputs produced through this work to develop our recommendations for Government themed around the areas of tools, data and governance which will be published in March 2020. We will provide an initial list of tools and approaches to guide the assessment and standards development, however further work will be needed to ensure this has sufficient coverage to capture all the key approaches available. The focus of our work in this space is financial services and recruitment. Therefore, we would expect this work to provide good coverage and analysis of tools that are explicitly aimed at these two sectors.
